touches.text: The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else (Akien, 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02).
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve, and the tester (11; Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29). (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)

chain: the grammar every chart stage speaks. Stays in tools/: CodeMother is its heaviest user, not its only one (base, tester, rehearsal, build_inspector, proof_coverage, aider_shim, skills/chart also import it) (Q#50, Akien 2026-10-29).
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.
proof_coverage: joins a ticket's falsifier clauses to the proofs that cover them and the seals that ran green. → Tester
